newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia manganese firm resumes limited output.
newsitem.headline: Georgia manganese firm resumes limited output.

text.p: Georgian manganese producer AO Chiaturmarganets which halted output at the start of the year has resumed production, but only at a limited rate, a source in the economic section of the state administration said on Friday.
"We are seriously concerned about the situation at Chiaturmarganets," said Giga Chogovadze.
He said the company was still in serious financial difficulty, worsened by constant cuts in electricity supplies and large debts.
The company was built around the Chiatursk metal ore combine and processes manganese from Georgia's largest deposit of the metal. The government holds a controlling share stake.

Chogovadze said that a number of foreign companies, including Samancor of South Africa, had expressed an interest in restoring production levels and in exporting manganese from Georgia to world markets.
"But so far we have not decided whether we will hold a tender or whether we will simply hand over management rights to foreign investors," he said.

The plant produced 15,000 tonnes of manganese concentrates last year, when output was sharply reduced due to a lack of finance. In Soviet times the company produced up to 1.7 to 1.8 million tonnes annually. --Dzhana Sommerlund, Tblisi Newsroom +8832 983 961
